children: National Fuel Gas Company plans to assess a potential plan to separate into two publicly-traded companies, with its board aiming to complete its evaluation by Oct. 15.
Under the plan, National Fuel would separate its integrated upstream and gathering (IUG) business, creating two companies with distinct focuses, the company said Thursday.
National Fuel would be a fully-regulated natural gas business, while IUG would be an integrated Appalachian natural gas business.

National Fuel Chief Executive David Bauer said that while the company has benefited from its diversified business model for years, the capital markets and operating environment of its regulated and non-regulated natural gas businesses have evolved.

"With the expected closing of our Ohio gas utility acquisition next month, each business will be a scaled platform with distinct strategic priorities, organic growth opportunities, capital needs, and investment profiles," Bauer said.
If the plan is approved, National Fuel would distribute IUG shares to National Fuel shareholders in a manner intended to be tax-free for the company and its shareholders, the company said.
